architecture.summary: SO-09 adds the tenant fleet operations: the weekly organization sweep and the daily fleet summary in the hosted control plane, and the operator fleet script (script/fleet/, a new operator CLI container outside src) that lists, requests, upgrades, suspends, resumes, deletes, and summarizes tenants. TenantPlatform gains five operations with closed result unions (deployImage, suspendService, resumeService, memoryUse, restartCount); the new public contract OrganizationInventory of tenants is implemented by workos, a new type-only edge workos -> tenants, and the rules forbid tenants -> workos. In the server only the sweeps use the new parts: delete, memoryUse, and restartCount, the fleet read, and the deleted mark; deploy, suspend, resume, their marks, the digest record, and the revive have callers only in the fleet script. The sweep deletes a tenant only when the complete WorkOS list leaves the organization out and the read by ID answers 404; a failed page deletes nothing, and creating and deploying rows wait. Each fleet change names the state and the service that it starts from, and the live record of the provisioner and of the fleet resume names its service too, so a stale write of a slow operation moves instead of changing a replacement row with a new service (manager decision of 31 October 2026). The deletion authority has a bound (manager decision of 28 October 2026): an empty list, or more than 2 rows that are not deleted and absent from the list, deletes nothing and gives one Organization sweep stopped line with reason, rows, organizations, and absent, so a WorkOS key of another environment or a defect of the list read cannot delete the fleet; the operator deletes by hand with the fleet script. The fleet writes share a deploy wait in tenants: an upgrade follows the deploy that the 201 answer names, stops on a newer deploy with another ID, and records the digest only when the live deploy names it; after a 202 answer and after each resume the first new deploy counts, with an unconfirmed identity (manager decision of 31 October 2026). Until SO-10 connects the resume of the gateway, only the fleet resume brings back a suspended tenant (owner decision of 31 October 2026). New external use: Render deploy by image digest, suspend, resume, memory metrics, and service events; WorkOS organization list, read by ID, and memberships. New contracts: the log lines Tenant fleet summary, Organization sweep, Tenant removal record and failed, which the SO-11 monitors read, and the setting TENANT_SWEEP_HOUR_UTC, read only with MCP_TENANTS_ENABLED=true. The sweeps share the SQL runtime slots and the Render limits with the provisioner. Five registry views change: Context, C4 containers hosted (operator CLI container), the tenant registry view (WorkOS adapter, new calls), the collaboration overview, and the new weekly organization sweep scenario. The rules file declares the edge, the public module, and the forbidden edge; the test gate policy adds the new suites; no package, migration, or deployment unit changes.
